model_year.note: Label for the year whose specs are quoted. Not a statement about availability.

length_in.note: 2027 IONIQ 5 Features and Specifications, Exterior (inches), 'All' column; no XRT exception is given for length. Text extraction offsets values one row from labels (sources/hyundai-2027-ioniq-5-specs-features.txt); the reading is confirmed by C/D's figures. Ioniq 5 N (folded in) is longer: C/D's 2025 Ioniq 5 N test lists 185.6 in (sources/cd-hyundai-ioniq-5-n-2026.html); no Hyundai figure fetched for the N.

width_in.note: 'Overall Width'; the sheet doesn't say whether mirrors are included. C/D lists the same figure as width without mirrors. Ioniq 5 N: 76.4 in per C/D's 2025 test.

awd.label: SE, SEL, XRT, Limited
awd.note: 27MY IONIQ 5 model list, Drivetrain column (prices not recorded). Ioniq 5 N is AWD per C/D.

charge_port.note: 2027 press kit: 'standard North American Charging Standard (NACS) port'; 'Native NACS charging port'. Pricing sheet lists 'NACS --> CCS Adapter' in the base package. Ioniq 5 N (folded in): Hyundai's Dec. 23, 2024 adapter release lists the '2025 IONIQ 5 N' among CCS-port models (sources/hyundai-api-2025-kona-electric-releases.json); no N port source for 2026 or later.

supercharger_access.note: 2027 press kit: 'standard North American Charging Standard (NACS) port'; 'Native NACS charging port'. Pricing sheet lists 'NACS --> CCS Adapter' in the base package. Ioniq 5 N (folded in): Hyundai's Dec. 23, 2024 adapter release lists the '2025 IONIQ 5 N' among CCS-port models (sources/hyundai-api-2025-kona-electric-releases.json); no N port source for 2026 or later.

cross_check.note: Tesla lists Hyundai among manufacturers with access to NACS Superchargers; 'For new vehicles that are NACS-equipped, no adapter will be necessary.' Read through headless Edge (sources/tesla-supercharging-other-evs-rendered.html); curl gets HTTP 403.

us_status.note: 27MY pricing 'Effective: August 3, 2026'. The press kit doesn't give an on-sale date; the effective pricing date is used as the nearest sourced indicator. 2026 model is the year ranked by C/D, MotorTrend and Edmunds.

entries.applies_to: SE RWD, SEL RWD, Limited RWD

epa_range.note: EPA lists no 2027 Ioniq 5 N, so the folded-in N has no range here. Trim mapping from Hyundai's spec sheet ('SE/SEL: 290 miles', 'Limited: 269', 'XRT: 259').

trims.note: 27MY pricing model list; XRT AWD also comes 'w/ Tow Hitch'. Ioniq 5 N (folded in) has no 2027 listing.

entries.note: C/D test sheet 'Peak DC Fast-Charge Rate: 250 kW' (84.0-kWh dual-motor car). Hyundai's own sheet gives charger ratings only: 'kW rates listed are max rates for chargers - not actual vehicle charging rates'.

'DC Fast Charging: >250kW (800V) (from 10% 80% charge)' 20 min, listed under 'w/CCS Adapter'. charger_kw is the stated floor. The press kit also says 'approximately 24 minutes' via CCS adapter on a 350-kW charger.
'DC Fast Charging: 150kW (400V)' 30 min, listed under 'Charge Time: NACS'.

entries.applies_to: SE AWD, SEL AWD, XRT AWD, Limited AWD
entries.note: 27MY pricing lists 'Heat pump (heater)' in the AWD versions' equipment; the specs sheet's Heat Pump row reads 'AWD-only' for SE, SEL, XRT and Limited (the row is offset by one line in the text layer).
Inferred from 'AWD-only'; the RWD equipment lists don't include it.

cargo_cu_ft.note: 'Cargo capacity, rear seats up' 26.3 (SAE); 'rear seats folded down' 58.5 (SAE); frunk 0.85. Read from staggered columns.

turning_circle_ft.note: Hyundai's sheet has a 'Turning Diameter (curb to curb, ft)' row but its value isn't in the PDF text layer; C/D figure used.

height_in.note: 'Overall Height' 63.0 (64.0 XRT), read from staggered columns.

ground_clearance_in.note: 'Minimum Ground Clearance' 6.1 (7.0 XRT), read from staggered columns.

highway_tests.note: C/D 75-mph highway range test. Temperature not stated.
C/D 75-mph highway range test. Temperature not stated.

supercharger_reports.claim: Hyundai's 2027 spec sheet lists 10-80% in 30 min on a 150 kW (400V) charger under 'Charge Time: NACS', against 20 min on a >250 kW (800V) charger via CCS adapter.

notes.text: Hyundai's own figures: 10-80% takes about 30 minutes on a 400-volt charger such as a Tesla Supercharger, against about 20 on the fastest 800-volt chargers.
Peak DC rate is from Car and Driver's test sheet; Hyundai publishes charger ratings, not the car's peak.
